excerpt: Searchlight was a San Francisco AI talent intelligence startup founded by twins Anna and Kerry Wang. Multiverse acquired it in April 2024 and wound down its recruiting product.
content:
Searchlight was a talent intelligence and skills assessment platform. Companies used it to assess candidates and employees with AI, predict how well people would fit a role, and understand the skills in their workforce, with the aim of better hiring and closing skills gaps. Recruiter reported that its customers included Udemy, Zapier and Talkdesk.

Searchlight was founded in 2018 by twin sisters Anna Wang and Kerry Wang and went through Y Combinator in winter 2019; YC's directory lists it in San Francisco. Anna Wang's YC profile says Searchlight was backed by Accel at seed and Founders Fund in its Series A. On 8 April 2024 Multiverse, the UK workplace training and apprenticeship company, announced that it had acquired Searchlight for an undisclosed sum. Multiverse said it would use Searchlight's technology to build AI products for its own training services, and Recruiter reported that existing Searchlight customers would be served until their contracts ended, after which Multiverse would wind down Searchlight's recruitment services. Kerry Wang took a director of product role and Anna Wang a head of AI role at Multiverse at the time.

Searchlight's own website is no longer online, and the product is not sold separately, so there is no price to quote. Companies looking for similar tools today would compare skills-based hiring and talent intelligence platforms such as Eightfold, HireVue and TestGorilla.

We have not used Searchlight for this page. It brings together Searchlight's own website and the reporting linked under Sources, and says where each fact comes from. Nothing here is paid placement.
